meta.title: Mastering Serverless Applications with AWS Amplify
meta.author: John Doe

parts.title: The Evolution of Full Stack Development

sentences: This preface explains the **author's journey** and the **motivation** behind writing a book on **full-stack serverless development**.

Initially overwhelmed by the complexities of **software development**, **Nader Dabit** highlights how modern tools like **React Native** and cloud services such as **AWS Amplify** now empower **solo developers** to accomplish previously **team-driven tasks**.

This book is aimed at **developers** interested in **cloud computing** and looking to expand into **full-stack roles**, and also **CTOs** and **startup founders** keen on improving **developer efficiency** and **scalability**.

**AWS** saw an opportunity to create **Amplify Framework** to help developers, especially front-end ones, start building **cloud applications** easily by offering a simpler interface to interact with AWS services.

**Amplify CLI** acts as an entry point using simpler "**category names**" like **auth** instead of complex service names like **Amazon Cognito**, easing tasks like creating and configuring AWS services without leaving your **frontend environment**.
The **Amplify Client**, on the other hand, offers an **easy API for JavaScript** to interact with these services, making AWS more approachable for **client-side development**.
AWS **AppSync** is a managed **API layer** using **GraphQL**, simplifying application interaction with **data sources**.
Microsservices and third-party APIs create messy codes due to variability.
Centralized API gateways help by offering a unified interaction level for the client with all backend services.
**GraphQL** is a good candidate since it introduces **queries, mutations,** and **subscriptions** as consistent operations.
**AWS AppSync**, handles API management and security, making development easier with features like **real-time** and **offline support**.
In development, AWS **Amplify CLI** helps create and manage cloud services, letting developers deploy, modify or delete services intuitively.
Configuring Amplify involves installing it, then setting up identity credentials using the **IAM user**, and specifying your **AWS region** and username.
Creating apps mean setting parameters like **project name, environment,** and other specs appropriately to ensure smooth app functionality.
This process simplifies cloud computing development as emphasized in recent explorations and books on AWS technologies.

parts.title: Building a GraphQL API with DynamoDB using AWS Amplify

sentences: One can **build a GraphQL API** with AWS Amplify that interacts with **DynamoDB** to perform CRUD operations for a notes app.

GraphQL is a query language and runtime for APIs, introduced by Facebook, that allows clients to specify the exact data they need, improving efficiency by **reducing over-fetching** and **under-fetching** of data.
It offers better type safety compared to REST.
A GraphQL API consists of schemas, resolvers, and data sources.
GraphQL schemas are written in Schema Definition Language (SDL) and define the data models and operations like **queries, mutations**, and **subscriptions**—the latter updating data in real-time.
Queries fetch data, while mutations create, update, or delete it.
They map to HTTP methods, with GraphQL requests looking like JavaScript objects containing only keys.

parts.title: Creating a React App with GraphQL API Using AWS Amplify

sentences: To start building the **Notes app** with **GraphQL** using **AWS Amplify**, you first need to set up a **React application**.
Use **npx create-react-app** to create it, then install dependencies like **aws-amplify**, **antd**, and **uuid**.
In the app's root, initialize an **Amplify project** using **amplify init**.
Enter details such as the project's name and environment.
You'll select **javascript** as the app type and **react** as the framework.
This setup establishes a base for integrating the **GraphQL API**.
With the Amplify project ready, add the **GraphQL API** using **amplify add api**.
Configure initial settings such as the API name and the authorization type.
Opt for guided schema creation, which allows you to define the **GraphQL schema** interactively.
The schema defines a **Note** type with attributes like **id, name, description,** and **completed** status.
Annotate with **@model** to use Amplify's GraphQL Transform library, automating the creation of queries, mutations, and DynamoDB setup.
Deploy the configuration using **amplify push** to create the backend infrastructure.

parts.title: Implementing User Authentication and Real-Time Updates

sentences: In this guide, we are extending a React application to include user authentication using AWS Amplify and Amazon Cognito.
This involves creating user pools for user management (sign-up, sign-in, etc.) which handle user authentication seamlessly and scale with your application.
With the Amplify CLI and JavaScript client, we set up a fully managed authentication service.
We'll also utilize custom React components and Ant Design for a polished UI.
This approach enables the creation of protected routes that require sign-in, effectively implementing user access control.
Additionally, you can enhance app engagement with real-time updates through GraphQL subscriptions, allowing automatic updates of data like notes when they are modified, added, or deleted.
**Protected Routes:** The `protectedRoute` hook **checks** if a user is **signed in**.
If not, it redirects them to **another page** (like '/profile').
This means if you're not logged in, you can't access certain parts of the app.
**Custom Forms:** Instead of using Amplify's default, we're making our own custom forms for **signing up**, **signing in**, and **resetting passwords**.
We've created basic **component forms** like `SignIn` and `SignUp`, each with fields and **submission buttons**.
This allows for more control over how our forms look and work.
In **Form.js**, we've set up functions like **signIn**, **signUp**, and **confirmSignUp** to handle user authentication with **AWS Amplify**.
These functions interface with the **Auth** class to interact with the backend authentication services, efficiently managing sign-ins and sign-ups.
The **signIn** function uniquely involves the **setUser** callback, allowing the app to update and present user-specific information once authentication is successful.
We also implemented **updateForm**, a helper function to streamline form state updates, maintaining the existing form state while incorporating new input values.
This is hooked into our React components to keep the state updated across various user inputs, enhancing user experience by ensuring data consistency and ease of state handling.

parts.title: Setting up REST API with AWS Amplify

sentences: A **REST API** is **set up** using AWS Amplify and **Lambda**.
The **Lambda function** integrates with an **Express server**, enabling us to define routes and perform actions like GET, POST, and DELETE on **DynamoDB**.
We establish an **authentication** service, utilizing the **Cognito** SDK to manage user groups.
Only users in the **"Admin"** group can perform certain actions for enhanced security.
This is achieved through `canPerformAction` and `getGroupsForUser`, which check a user's permissions and group memberships.
Laying the groundwork for building our app by creating different components necessary for our frontend.
**Admin.js** will hold the admin dashboard for creating new items, while **Container.js** will provide a consistent layout style.
**Main.js** will list the items for sale, and **Nav.js** will manage navigation, showing an "Admin" link only for authorized users.
**Profile.js** features basic user authentication, allowing users to sign out.
**Router.js** will manage the app's routing between different pages.
Finally, **checkUser.js** will verify if a user is an admin.
We start by creating these components and importing necessary libraries in **src/index.js**, including **Amplify** for AWS integration and **Ant Design** for styling.
**Amplify DataStore** is a client-side SDK that works with **GraphQL APIs** to store data locally, sync it online automatically, manage **conflict detection**, and ensure data persistence offline.
Operations include **saving**, **reading**, **updating**, **deleting** data, and **observing changes** for real-time functionality.
DataStore simplifies managing both local and remote data, **syncing** when connected while queuing changes during offline mode.
It also allows applying **predicate filters** for data querying, using fields and conditions supported by **DynamoDB**.

parts.title: Building a Real-Time Offline Message Board

sentences: Whenever there's an **update** or **new entry** in your message board, the app will trigger a subscription that listens for **real-time changes** to keep in sync with data from other users.
We're building a **React app** using Amplify that supports offline-first capabilities.
The app lets you create messages while offline.
When online, these messages automatically **sync** with the backend.
By using the **Amplify DataStore API**, we can effectively manage **real-time** data handling and offline data persistence.
In this documentation, we've explored how to host applications using **Amplify Console** with both **CLI-based** and **Git-based** deployments.
**CLI-based deployments** involve pushing your local project directly to Amplify Console.
To get started, create a React application, configure Amplify, and add authentication.
Use `amplify add hosting` to prepare for deployment, and finally, deploy using `amplify publish`.
This method allows quick updates by re-running the publish command whenever changes are ready.
**Git-based deployments** use a Github repository to manage and deploy applications.
By linking Amplify Console with the repo, you can automatically build and deploy new changes whenever a commit is pushed to the master branch.
This integration allows seamless **CI/CD** setup and enables branch-specific access control.
You can also add **custom domains**, ensuring your app is accessible with a personalized URL.
The Amplify Console offers a robust solution for deploying both frontend and backend components with options for **access control** and **domain management**.
